request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Sex: Male
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital Course:

The patient, an 18-year-old male with no significant past medical history, was admitted to the emergency department with complaints of suprapubic and periumbilical pain, accompanied by nausea for one day. Physical examination revealed mild tenderness to palpation in the periumbilical, right lower quadrant, and left upper quadrant regions. Respiratory rate, heart rate, and blood pressure were within normal limits, but complete blood count revealed leukocytosis with a left shift.

A CT exam was performed to rule out any underlying causes of the aforementioned symptoms, demonstrating a dilated and hyperenhancing retrocecal appendix containing a form of calcified materials within it. Moreover, small air collections were identified anterior to the right and left common iliac arteries, and posterior to both psoas muscles in the retroperitoneal cavity of the abdomen.

The patient was taken to the operating room for an appendectomy, during which an additional inflamed appendix, and evidence of minor perforation into the retroperitoneum were found. Surgical team continued with appendectomy in view of inferior incision area revealing no pathologic process in the retroperitoneal cavity.

The patient was monitored in the post-operative care unit and demonstrated no post-operative complications. The patient was discharged the following day in stable condition.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Instructions:

The patient is advised to take all prescribed medications and attend follow-up appointments as scheduled. Discharge instructions and the post-operative care plan have been explained to the patient in detail before being discharged.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
CODE: K35

The principal diagnosis is acute appendicitis. The patient had an appendectomy, and the surgery confirmed an inflamed appendix with minor perforation. Category K35 covers acute appendicitis, and the more specific subcategories (K35.2 to K35.8) are not needed for a three-character answer.
